newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Job creation not at odds with stability-Brown.
newsitem.headline: Job creation not at odds with stability-Brown.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Tuesday that the Amsterdam summit meeting of European leaders had demonstrated that action to create jobs was not at odds with stability policies.
"We have shown that action to create jobs is not incompatible with stability or with the convergence criteria (for European monetary union)" he told reporters.
"Amsterdam has shown that there is a real agenda about jobs and growth in Europe," Brown added.
EU leaders on Monday introduced a resolution aimed at boosting employment and promised to hold a special jobs summit later this year.

Brown said he wanted to use next year's meeting of leaders from the world's seven largest industrialised powers (G7), which is being hosted by Britain, to look at ways of marrying economic growth while at the same time safeguarding social rights.
"We want to see how we can achieve growth with also a sense of social fairness," Brown said. The G7 leaders are due to meet in the United States later this week for their annual meeting.
Brown said with some 18.5 million people unemployed in the 15-nation EU, European leaders would be failing in their duty if they did not put jobs at the top of their agenda.
